# Skeleton: Autonomous software agents to 2027-09-17

World: arn518-unattended-20260917-c

## Scope and method
This first-pass skeleton records only facts already determined by current primary sources: enacted rules with future effect, dated official commitments, shipped or documented product capabilities, and funded/announced infrastructure commitments. It does not forecast adoption, capability, revenues, accidents, or policy outcomes.

## Determined event nodes
1. **slow** — The EU Artificial Intelligence Act is in force and its general application date is 2 August 2026; prohibited-practices and AI-literacy obligations applied from 2 February 2025 and GPAI-model governance obligations applied from 2 August 2025, creating a live compliance baseline for autonomous software-agent providers serving the EU.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai"]
2. **slow** — Under the EU AI Act implementation timeline published by the European Commission, transparency rules for AI-generated or manipulated content came into effect in August 2026, including duties relevant to agent systems that generate text, audio, images, video, or deepfakes for users.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai"]
3. **slow** — The EU AI Act rules for AI systems used in listed high-risk areas, including critical infrastructure, education, employment, migration, asylum, border control, administration of justice, and democratic processes, are scheduled to apply from 2 December 2027, after this world horizon but already setting a compliance runway by 2027-09-17.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai"]
4. **slow** — The EU Data Act entered into force on 11 January 2024 and applied from 12 September 2025, establishing cross-sector rules on access to and use of data, user access to connected-device data, data sharing, and cloud switching that are already part of the data environment for software agents.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/data-act"]
5. **slow** — The EU Cyber Resilience Act entered into force on 10 December 2024; manufacturers, importers, and distributors must comply with the main obligations from 11 December 2027, while vulnerability-reporting obligations apply from 11 September 2026, affecting agent products with digital elements before the horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cyber-resilience-act"]
6. **slow** — The Colorado Artificial Intelligence Act was enacted in 2024 with a stated effective date of 1 February 2026, imposing duties on developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to use reasonable care to protect consumers from algorithmic discrimination.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://leg.colorado.gov/bills/sb24-205"]
7. **slow** — NIST has published the AI Risk Management Framework and the Generative AI Profile, providing an official U.S. voluntary risk-management baseline already available for organizations deploying agentic systems before 2027-09-17.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework"]
8. **slow** — The U.S. federal executive order of 23 January 2025, Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence, revoked Executive Order 14110 and directed federal agencies to review, suspend, revise, or rescind actions that conflict with the new AI policy.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/01/removing-barriers-to-american-leadership-in-artificial-intelligence/"]
9. **mid** — OpenAI has released a Responses API, built-in tools including web search, file search, and computer use, and an Agents SDK for orchestrating single-agent and multi-agent workflows, so an agent-building stack is already generally documented for developers before the 2027 horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://openai.com/index/new-tools-for-building-agents/","https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/agents"]
10. **mid** — Anthropic released Claude computer use in public beta in October 2024, documenting that the model can view a screen, move a cursor, click buttons, and type text through a tool interface, establishing browser/desktop-control capability as an available agent primitive before 2027.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://www.anthropic.com/news/3-5-models-and-computer-use","https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/computer-use/overview"]
11. **mid** — Microsoft announced in October 2024 that autonomous agents in Copilot Studio would move from private preview to public preview at Microsoft Ignite 2024, making enterprise agent creation and management a shipped Microsoft product path before the 2027 horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2024/10/21/new-autonomous-agents-scale-your-team-like-never-before/"]
12. **mid** — GitHub Copilot coding agent is documented as a feature that can be assigned GitHub issues, works in its own development environment, pushes commits, and opens pull requests for human review, so asynchronous software-development agents already exist as a productized workflow before 2027.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/about-copilot-coding-agent","https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/github-copilot-coding-agent-in-public-preview/"]
13. **mid** — OpenAI announced the Stargate Project on 21 January 2025 as a new company intending to invest 500 billion dollars over four years in U.S. AI infrastructure for OpenAI, with 100 billion dollars beginning immediately and initial equity funders including SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle, and MGX.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://openai.com/index/announcing-the-stargate-project/"]
14. **mid** — OpenAI stated that Arm, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Oracle, and OpenAI are initial technology partners in the Stargate Project, fixing part of the compute-supply consortium available to OpenAI agent products before the 2027 horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://openai.com/index/announcing-the-stargate-project/"]

## Load-bearing uncertainty axes (ADR-006)
These are not determined facts; they are orthogonal dimensions on which 2027-09-17 can genuinely fork.

1. **Agent autonomy ceiling in production software work** — consensus pole: agents remain strongest as scoped copilots/asynchronous junior contributors whose outputs are reviewed by humans, rather than trusted end-to-end owners of major systems.
2. **Enterprise permissioning and liability tolerance** — consensus pole: organizations allow agents to operate inside constrained sandboxes with audit trails, approval gates, and limited credentials, rather than broad unsupervised authority across systems of record.
3. **Compute and model cost trajectory** — consensus pole: frontier-capability agents become cheaper and faster, but high-reliability long-horizon agent runs still face meaningful cost/latency limits and supply concentration.
4. **Regulatory fragmentation versus harmonization** — consensus pole: the EU AI Act and sector/state rules create compliance workstreams, but there is no single globally harmonized agent-governance regime by the horizon.
5. **Security and misuse pressure** — consensus pole: agentic tools materially expand both defensive automation and offensive/scam automation, so security controls and identity/provenance mechanisms become central deployment constraints.

## Bounded deeper exploration: three futures to sample, without predicting
The determined facts above can support three distinct future explorations:
- **Regulated enterprise copilots:** EU/Colorado/NIST baselines and enterprise productization channel agents into auditable workflows with limited autonomy.
- **Software-development acceleration:** GitHub/OpenAI/Anthropic/Microsoft primitives make asynchronous coding and computer-use agents a common development substrate, bounded by review and security gates.
- **Compute-rich frontier agents:** Stargate-style infrastructure and cloud/accelerator consortia expand available capacity for more capable agent services, while cost, safety, and governance remain the sampled uncertainties.

# Skeleton: Autonomous software agents to 2027-09-17

World: arn518-unattended-20260917-c

## Scope and method
This first-pass skeleton records only facts already determined by current primary sources: enacted rules with future effect, dated official commitments, shipped or documented product capabilities, and funded/announced infrastructure commitments. It does not forecast adoption, capability, revenues, accidents, or policy outcomes.

## Determined event nodes
1. **slow** — The EU Artificial Intelligence Act is in force and its general application date is 2 August 2026; prohibited-practices and AI-literacy obligations applied from 2 February 2025 and GPAI-model governance obligations applied from 2 August 2025, creating a live compliance baseline for autonomous software-agent providers serving the EU.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai"]
2. **slow** — Under the EU AI Act implementation timeline published by the European Commission, transparency rules for AI-generated or manipulated content came into effect in August 2026, including duties relevant to agent systems that generate text, audio, images, video, or deepfakes for users.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai"]
3. **slow** — The EU AI Act rules for AI systems used in listed high-risk areas, including critical infrastructure, education, employment, migration, asylum, border control, administration of justice, and democratic processes, are scheduled to apply from 2 December 2027, after this world horizon but already setting a compliance runway by 2027-09-17.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai"]
4. **slow** — The EU Data Act entered into force on 11 January 2024 and applied from 12 September 2025, establishing cross-sector rules on access to and use of data, user access to connected-device data, data sharing, and cloud switching that are already part of the data environment for software agents.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/data-act"]
5. **slow** — The EU Cyber Resilience Act entered into force on 10 December 2024; manufacturers, importers, and distributors must comply with the main obligations from 11 December 2027, while vulnerability-reporting obligations apply from 11 September 2026, affecting agent products with digital elements before the horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cyber-resilience-act"]
6. **slow** — The Colorado Artificial Intelligence Act was enacted in 2024 with a stated effective date of 1 February 2026, imposing duties on developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to use reasonable care to protect consumers from algorithmic discrimination.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://leg.colorado.gov/bills/sb24-205"]
7. **slow** — NIST has published the AI Risk Management Framework and the Generative AI Profile, providing an official U.S. voluntary risk-management baseline already available for organizations deploying agentic systems before 2027-09-17.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework"]
8. **slow** — The U.S. federal executive order of 23 January 2025, Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence, revoked Executive Order 14110 and directed federal agencies to review, suspend, revise, or rescind actions that conflict with the new AI policy.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/01/removing-barriers-to-american-leadership-in-artificial-intelligence/"]
9. **mid** — OpenAI has released a Responses API, built-in tools including web search, file search, and computer use, and an Agents SDK for orchestrating single-agent and multi-agent workflows, so an agent-building stack is already generally documented for developers before the 2027 horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://openai.com/index/new-tools-for-building-agents/","https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/agents"]
10. **mid** — Anthropic released Claude computer use in public beta in October 2024, documenting that the model can view a screen, move a cursor, click buttons, and type text through a tool interface, establishing browser/desktop-control capability as an available agent primitive before 2027.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://www.anthropic.com/news/3-5-models-and-computer-use","https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/computer-use/overview"]
11. **mid** — Microsoft announced in October 2024 that autonomous agents in Copilot Studio would move from private preview to public preview at Microsoft Ignite 2024, making enterprise agent creation and management a shipped Microsoft product path before the 2027 horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2024/10/21/new-autonomous-agents-scale-your-team-like-never-before/"]
12. **mid** — GitHub Copilot coding agent is documented as a feature that can be assigned GitHub issues, works in its own development environment, pushes commits, and opens pull requests for human review, so asynchronous software-development agents already exist as a productized workflow before 2027.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/about-copilot-coding-agent","https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/github-copilot-coding-agent-in-public-preview/"]
13. **mid** — OpenAI announced the Stargate Project on 21 January 2025 as a new company intending to invest 500 billion dollars over four years in U.S. AI infrastructure for OpenAI, with 100 billion dollars beginning immediately and initial equity funders including SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle, and MGX.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://openai.com/index/announcing-the-stargate-project/"]
14. **mid** — OpenAI stated that Arm, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Oracle, and OpenAI are initial technology partners in the Stargate Project, fixing part of the compute-supply consortium available to OpenAI agent products before the 2027 horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://openai.com/index/announcing-the-stargate-project/"]

## Load-bearing uncertainty axes (ADR-006)
These are not determined facts; they are orthogonal dimensions on which 2027-09-17 can genuinely fork.

1. **Agent autonomy ceiling in production software work** — consensus pole: agents remain strongest as scoped copilots/asynchronous junior contributors whose outputs are reviewed by humans, rather than trusted end-to-end owners of major systems.
2. **Enterprise permissioning and liability tolerance** — consensus pole: organizations allow agents to operate inside constrained sandboxes with audit trails, approval gates, and limited credentials, rather than broad unsupervised authority across systems of record.
3. **Compute and model cost trajectory** — consensus pole: frontier-capability agents become cheaper and faster, but high-reliability long-horizon agent runs still face meaningful cost/latency limits and supply concentration.
4. **Regulatory fragmentation versus harmonization** — consensus pole: the EU AI Act and sector/state rules create compliance workstreams, but there is no single globally harmonized agent-governance regime by the horizon.
5. **Security and misuse pressure** — consensus pole: agentic tools materially expand both defensive automation and offensive/scam automation, so security controls and identity/provenance mechanisms become central deployment constraints.

## Bounded deeper exploration: three futures to sample, without predicting
The determined facts above can support three distinct future explorations:
- **Regulated enterprise copilots:** EU/Colorado/NIST baselines and enterprise productization channel agents into auditable workflows with limited autonomy.
- **Software-development acceleration:** GitHub/OpenAI/Anthropic/Microsoft primitives make asynchronous coding and computer-use agents a common development substrate, bounded by review and security gates.
- **Compute-rich frontier agents:** Stargate-style infrastructure and cloud/accelerator consortia expand available capacity for more capable agent services, while cost, safety, and governance remain the sampled uncertainties.

## Scope and method
This first-pass skeleton records only facts already determined by current primary sources: enacted rules with future effect, dated official commitments, shipped or documented product capabilities, and funded/announced infrastructure commitments.    - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai"]
2. **slow** — Under the EU AI Act implementation timeline published by the European Commission, transparency rules for AI-generated or manipulated content came into effect in August 2026, including duties relevant to agent systems that generate text, audio, images, video, or deepfakes for users.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai"]
3. **slow** — The EU AI Act rules for AI systems used in listed high-risk areas, including critical infrastructure, education, employment, migration, asylum, border control, administration of justice, and democratic processes, are scheduled to apply from 2 December 2027, after this world horizon but already setting a compliance runway by 2027-09-17.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai"]
4. **slow** — The EU Data Act entered into force on 11 January 2024 and applied from 12 September 2025, establishing cross-sector rules on access to and use of data, user access to connected-device data, data sharing, and cloud switching that are already part of the data environment for software agents.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/data-act"]
5. **slow** — The EU Cyber Resilience Act entered into force on 10 December 2024; manufacturers, importers, and distributors must comply with the main obligations from 11 December 2027, while vulnerability-reporting obligations apply from 11 September 2026, affecting agent products with digital elements before the horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cyber-resilience-act"]
6. **slow** — The Colorado Artificial Intelligence Act was enacted in 2024 with a stated effective date of 1 February 2026, imposing duties on developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to use reasonable care to protect consumers from algorithmic discrimination.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://leg.colorado.gov/bills/sb24-205"]
7. **slow** — NIST has published the AI Risk Management Framework and the Generative AI Profile, providing an official U.S. voluntary risk-management baseline already available for organizations deploying agentic systems before 2027-09-17.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework"]
8. **slow** — The U.S. federal executive order of 23 January 2025, Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence, revoked Executive Order 14110 and directed federal agencies to review, suspend, revise, or rescind actions that conflict with the new AI policy.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/01/removing-barriers-to-american-leadership-in-artificial-intelligence/"]
9. **mid** — OpenAI has released a Responses API, built-in tools including web search, file search, and computer use, and an Agents SDK for orchestrating single-agent and multi-agent workflows, so an agent-building stack is already generally documented for developers before the 2027 horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://openai.com/index/new-tools-for-building-agents/","https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/agents"]
10. **mid** — Anthropic released Claude computer use in public beta in October 2024, documenting that the model can view a screen, move a cursor, click buttons, and type text through a tool interface, establishing browser/desktop-control capability as an available agent primitive before 2027.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://www.anthropic.com/news/3-5-models-and-computer-use","https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/computer-use/overview"]
11. **mid** — Microsoft announced in October 2024 that autonomous agents in Copilot Studio would move from private preview to public preview at Microsoft Ignite 2024, making enterprise agent creation and management a shipped Microsoft product path before the 2027 horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2024/10/21/new-autonomous-agents-scale-your-team-like-never-before/"]
12. **mid** — GitHub Copilot coding agent is documented as a feature that can be assigned GitHub issues, works in its own development environment, pushes commits, and opens pull requests for human review, so asynchronous software-development agents already exist as a productized workflow before 2027.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/about-copilot-coding-agent","https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/github-copilot-coding-agent-in-public-preview/"]
13. **mid** — OpenAI announced the Stargate Project on 21 January 2025 as a new company intending to invest 500 billion dollars over four years in U.S. AI infrastructure for OpenAI, with 100 billion dollars beginning immediately and initial equity funders including SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle, and MGX.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://openai.com/index/announcing-the-stargate-project/"]
14. **mid** — OpenAI stated that Arm, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Oracle, and OpenAI are initial technology partners in the Stargate Project, fixing part of the compute-supply consortium available to OpenAI agent products before the 2027 horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://openai.com/index/announcing-the-stargate-project/"]

## Load-bearing uncertainty axes (ADR-006)
These are not determined facts; they are orthogonal dimensions on which 2027-09-17 can genuinely fork.

1. **Agent autonomy ceiling in production software work** — consensus pole: agents remain strongest as scoped copilots/asynchronous junior contributors whose outputs are reviewed by humans, rather than trusted end-to-end owners of major systems.
2. **Enterprise permissioning and liability tolerance** — consensus pole: organizations allow agents to operate inside constrained sandboxes with audit trails, approval gates, and limited credentials, rather than broad unsupervised authority across systems of record.
3. **Compute and model cost trajectory** — consensus pole: frontier-capability agents become cheaper and faster, but high-reliability long-horizon agent runs still face meaningful cost/latency limits and supply concentration.
4. **Regulatory fragmentation versus harmonization** — consensus pole: the EU AI Act and sector/state rules create compliance workstreams, but there is no single globally harmonized agent-governance regime by the horizon.
5. **Security and misuse pressure** — consensus pole: agentic tools materially expand both defensive automation and offensive/scam automation, so security controls and identity/provenance mechanisms become central deployment constraints.

## Bounded deeper exploration: three futures to sample, without predicting
The determined facts above can support three distinct future explorations:
- **Regulated enterprise copilots:** EU/Colorado/NIST baselines and enterprise productization channel agents into auditable workflows with limited autonomy.
- **Software-development acceleration:** GitHub/OpenAI/Anthropic/Microsoft primitives make asynchronous coding and computer-use agents a common development substrate, bounded by review and security gates.
- **Compute-rich frontier agents:** Stargate-style infrastructure and cloud/accelerator consortia expand available capacity for more capable agent services, while cost, safety, and governance remain the sampled uncertainties.

This first-pass skeleton records only facts already determined by current primary sources: enacted rules with future effect, dated official commitments, shipped or documented product capabilities, and funded/announced infrastructure commitments. 1. **slow** — The EU Artificial Intelligence Act is in force and its general application date is 2 August 2026; prohibited-practices and AI-literacy obligations applied from 2 February 2025 and GPAI-model governance obligations applied from 2 August 2025, creating a live compliance baseline for autonomous software-agent providers serving the EU.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai"]
2. **slow** — Under the EU AI Act implementation timeline published by the European Commission, transparency rules for AI-generated or manipulated content came into effect in August 2026, including duties relevant to agent systems that generate text, audio, images, video, or deepfakes for users.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai"]
3. **slow** — The EU AI Act rules for AI systems used in listed high-risk areas, including critical infrastructure, education, employment, migration, asylum, border control, administration of justice, and democratic processes, are scheduled to apply from 2 December 2027, after this world horizon but already setting a compliance runway by 2027-09-17.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai"]
4. **slow** — The EU Data Act entered into force on 11 January 2024 and applied from 12 September 2025, establishing cross-sector rules on access to and use of data, user access to connected-device data, data sharing, and cloud switching that are already part of the data environment for software agents.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/data-act"]
5. **slow** — The EU Cyber Resilience Act entered into force on 10 December 2024; manufacturers, importers, and distributors must comply with the main obligations from 11 December 2027, while vulnerability-reporting obligations apply from 11 September 2026, affecting agent products with digital elements before the horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cyber-resilience-act"]
6. **slow** — The Colorado Artificial Intelligence Act was enacted in 2024 with a stated effective date of 1 February 2026, imposing duties on developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to use reasonable care to protect consumers from algorithmic discrimination.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://leg.colorado.gov/bills/sb24-205"]
7. **slow** — NIST has published the AI Risk Management Framework and the Generative AI Profile, providing an official U.S. voluntary risk-management baseline already available for organizations deploying agentic systems before 2027-09-17.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework"]
8. **slow** — The U.S. federal executive order of 23 January 2025, Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence, revoked Executive Order 14110 and directed federal agencies to review, suspend, revise, or rescind actions that conflict with the new AI policy.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/01/removing-barriers-to-american-leadership-in-artificial-intelligence/"]
9. **mid** — OpenAI has released a Responses API, built-in tools including web search, file search, and computer use, and an Agents SDK for orchestrating single-agent and multi-agent workflows, so an agent-building stack is already generally documented for developers before the 2027 horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://openai.com/index/new-tools-for-building-agents/","https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/agents"]
10. **mid** — Anthropic released Claude computer use in public beta in October 2024, documenting that the model can view a screen, move a cursor, click buttons, and type text through a tool interface, establishing browser/desktop-control capability as an available agent primitive before 2027.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://www.anthropic.com/news/3-5-models-and-computer-use","https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/computer-use/overview"]
11. **mid** — Microsoft announced in October 2024 that autonomous agents in Copilot Studio would move from private preview to public preview at Microsoft Ignite 2024, making enterprise agent creation and management a shipped Microsoft product path before the 2027 horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2024/10/21/new-autonomous-agents-scale-your-team-like-never-before/"]
12. **mid** — GitHub Copilot coding agent is documented as a feature that can be assigned GitHub issues, works in its own development environment, pushes commits, and opens pull requests for human review, so asynchronous software-development agents already exist as a productized workflow before 2027.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/about-copilot-coding-agent","https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/github-copilot-coding-agent-in-public-preview/"]
13. **mid** — OpenAI announced the Stargate Project on 21 January 2025 as a new company intending to invest 500 billion dollars over four years in U.S. AI infrastructure for OpenAI, with 100 billion dollars beginning immediately and initial equity funders including SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle, and MGX.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://openai.com/index/announcing-the-stargate-project/"]
14. **mid** — OpenAI stated that Arm, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Oracle, and OpenAI are initial technology partners in the Stargate Project, fixing part of the compute-supply consortium available to OpenAI agent products before the 2027 horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://openai.com/index/announcing-the-stargate-project/"]

## Load-bearing uncertainty axes (ADR-006)
These are not determined facts; they are orthogonal dimensions on which 2027-09-17 can genuinely fork.

1. **Agent autonomy ceiling in production software work** — consensus pole: agents remain strongest as scoped copilots/asynchronous junior contributors whose outputs are reviewed by humans, rather than trusted end-to-end owners of major systems.
2. **Enterprise permissioning and liability tolerance** — consensus pole: organizations allow agents to operate inside constrained sandboxes with audit trails, approval gates, and limited credentials, rather than broad unsupervised authority across systems of record.
3. **Compute and model cost trajectory** — consensus pole: frontier-capability agents become cheaper and faster, but high-reliability long-horizon agent runs still face meaningful cost/latency limits and supply concentration.
4. **Regulatory fragmentation versus harmonization** — consensus pole: the EU AI Act and sector/state rules create compliance workstreams, but there is no single globally harmonized agent-governance regime by the horizon.
5. **Security and misuse pressure** — consensus pole: agentic tools materially expand both defensive automation and offensive/scam automation, so security controls and identity/provenance mechanisms become central deployment constraints.

## Bounded deeper exploration: three futures to sample, without predicting
The determined facts above can support three distinct future explorations:
- **Regulated enterprise copilots:** EU/Colorado/NIST baselines and enterprise productization channel agents into auditable workflows with limited autonomy.
- **Software-development acceleration:** GitHub/OpenAI/Anthropic/Microsoft primitives make asynchronous coding and computer-use agents a common development substrate, bounded by review and security gates.
- **Compute-rich frontier agents:** Stargate-style infrastructure and cloud/accelerator consortia expand available capacity for more capable agent services, while cost, safety, and governance remain the sampled uncertainties.

These are not determined facts; they are orthogonal dimensions on which 2027-09-17 can genuinely fork.

1. **Agent autonomy ceiling in production software work** — consensus pole: agents remain strongest as scoped copilots/asynchronous junior contributors whose outputs are reviewed by humans, rather than trusted end-to-end owners of major systems.
2. **Enterprise permissioning and liability tolerance** — consensus pole: organizations allow agents to operate inside constrained sandboxes with audit trails, approval gates, and limited credentials, rather than broad unsupervised authority across systems of record.
3. **Compute and model cost trajectory** — consensus pole: frontier-capability agents become cheaper and faster, but high-reliability long-horizon agent runs still face meaningful cost/latency limits and supply concentration.
4. **Regulatory fragmentation versus harmonization** — consensus pole: the EU AI Act and sector/state rules create compliance workstreams, but there is no single globally harmonized agent-governance regime by the horizon.
5. **Security and misuse pressure** — consensus pole: agentic tools materially expand both defensive automation and offensive/scam automation, so security controls and identity/provenance mechanisms become central deployment constraints.

## Bounded deeper exploration: three futures to sample, without predicting
The determined facts above can support three distinct future explorations:
- **Regulated enterprise copilots:** EU/Colorado/NIST baselines and enterprise productization channel agents into auditable workflows with limited autonomy.
- **Software-development acceleration:** GitHub/OpenAI/Anthropic/Microsoft primitives make asynchronous coding and computer-use agents a common development substrate, bounded by review and security gates.
- **Compute-rich frontier agents:** Stargate-style infrastructure and cloud/accelerator consortia expand available capacity for more capable agent services, while cost, safety, and governance remain the sampled uncertainties.

This first-pass skeleton records only facts already determined by current primary sources: enacted rules with future effect, dated official commitments, shipped or documented product capabilities, and funded/announced infrastructure commitments.    - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai"]
3. **slow** — The EU AI Act rules for AI systems used in listed high-risk areas, including critical infrastructure, education, employment, migration, asylum, border control, administration of justice, and democratic processes, are scheduled to apply from 2 December 2027, after this world horizon but already setting a compliance runway by 2027-09-17.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai"]
4. **slow** — The EU Data Act entered into force on 11 January 2024 and applied from 12 September 2025, establishing cross-sector rules on access to and use of data, user access to connected-device data, data sharing, and cloud switching that are already part of the data environment for software agents.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/data-act"]
5. **slow** — The EU Cyber Resilience Act entered into force on 10 December 2024; manufacturers, importers, and distributors must comply with the main obligations from 11 December 2027, while vulnerability-reporting obligations apply from 11 September 2026, affecting agent products with digital elements before the horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cyber-resilience-act"]
6. **slow** — The Colorado Artificial Intelligence Act was enacted in 2024 with a stated effective date of 1 February 2026, imposing duties on developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to use reasonable care to protect consumers from algorithmic discrimination.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://leg.colorado.gov/bills/sb24-205"]
7. **slow** — NIST has published the AI Risk Management Framework and the Generative AI Profile, providing an official U.S. voluntary risk-management baseline already available for organizations deploying agentic systems before 2027-09-17.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework"]
8. **slow** — The U.S. federal executive order of 23 January 2025, Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence, revoked Executive Order 14110 and directed federal agencies to review, suspend, revise, or rescind actions that conflict with the new AI policy.

   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2024/10/21/new-autonomous-agents-scale-your-team-like-never-before/"]
12. **mid** — GitHub Copilot coding agent is documented as a feature that can be assigned GitHub issues, works in its own development environment, pushes commits, and opens pull requests for human review, so asynchronous software-development agents already exist as a productized workflow before 2027.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/about-copilot-coding-agent","https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/github-copilot-coding-agent-in-public-preview/"]
13. **mid** — OpenAI announced the Stargate Project on 21 January 2025 as a new company intending to invest 500 billion dollars over four years in U.S. AI infrastructure for OpenAI, with 100 billion dollars beginning immediately and initial equity funders including SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle, and MGX.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://openai.com/index/announcing-the-stargate-project/"]
14. **mid** — OpenAI stated that Arm, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Oracle, and OpenAI are initial technology partners in the Stargate Project, fixing part of the compute-supply consortium available to OpenAI agent products before the 2027 horizon.

These are not determined facts; they are orthogonal dimensions on which 2027-09-17 can genuinely fork.

1. **Agent autonomy ceiling in production software work** — consensus pole: agents remain strongest as scoped copilots/asynchronous junior contributors whose outputs are reviewed by humans, rather than trusted end-to-end owners of major systems.
2. **Enterprise permissioning and liability tolerance** — consensus pole: organizations allow agents to operate inside constrained sandboxes with audit trails, approval gates, and limited credentials, rather than broad unsupervised authority across systems of record.
3. **Compute and model cost trajectory** — consensus pole: frontier-capability agents become cheaper and faster, but high-reliability long-horizon agent runs still face meaningful cost/latency limits and supply concentration.
4. **Regulatory fragmentation versus harmonization** — consensus pole: the EU AI Act and sector/state rules create compliance workstreams, but there is no single globally harmonized agent-governance regime by the horizon.
5. **Security and misuse pressure** — consensus pole: agentic tools materially expand both defensive automation and offensive/scam automation, so security controls and identity/provenance mechanisms become central deployment constraints.

## Bounded deeper exploration: three futures to sample, without predicting
The determined facts above can support three distinct future explorations:

- **Compute-rich frontier agents:** Stargate-style infrastructure and cloud/accelerator consortia expand available capacity for more capable agent services, while cost, safety, and governance remain the sampled uncertainties.

# Skeleton: Autonomous software agents to 2027-09-17

World: arn518-unattended-20260917-c

## Scope and method
This first-pass skeleton records only facts already determined by current primary sources: enacted rules with future effect, dated official commitments, shipped or documented product capabilities, and funded/announced infrastructure commitments. It does not forecast adoption, capability, revenues, accidents, or policy outcomes.

## Determined event nodes
1. **slow** — The EU Artificial Intelligence Act is in force and its general application date is 2 August 2026; prohibited-practices and AI-literacy obligations applied from 2 February 2025 and GPAI-model governance obligations applied from 2 August 2025, creating a live compliance baseline for autonomous software-agent providers serving the EU.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai"]
2. **slow** — Under the EU AI Act implementation timeline published by the European Commission, transparency rules for AI-generated or manipulated content came into effect in August 2026, including duties relevant to agent systems that generate text, audio, images, video, or deepfakes for users.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai"]
3. **slow** — The EU AI Act rules for AI systems used in listed high-risk areas, including critical infrastructure, education, employment, migration, asylum, border control, administration of justice, and democratic processes, are scheduled to apply from 2 December 2027, after this world horizon but already setting a compliance runway by 2027-09-17.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/regulatory-framework-ai"]
4. **slow** — The EU Data Act entered into force on 11 January 2024 and applied from 12 September 2025, establishing cross-sector rules on access to and use of data, user access to connected-device data, data sharing, and cloud switching that are already part of the data environment for software agents.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/data-act"]
5. **slow** — The EU Cyber Resilience Act entered into force on 10 December 2024; manufacturers, importers, and distributors must comply with the main obligations from 11 December 2027, while vulnerability-reporting obligations apply from 11 September 2026, affecting agent products with digital elements before the horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu/en/policies/cyber-resilience-act"]
6. **slow** — The Colorado Artificial Intelligence Act was enacted in 2024 with a stated effective date of 1 February 2026, imposing duties on developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to use reasonable care to protect consumers from algorithmic discrimination.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://leg.colorado.gov/bills/sb24-205"]
7. **slow** — NIST has published the AI Risk Management Framework and the Generative AI Profile, providing an official U.S. voluntary risk-management baseline already available for organizations deploying agentic systems before 2027-09-17.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://www.nist.gov/itl/ai-risk-management-framework"]
8. **slow** — The U.S. federal executive order of 23 January 2025, Removing Barriers to American Leadership in Artificial Intelligence, revoked Executive Order 14110 and directed federal agencies to review, suspend, revise, or rescind actions that conflict with the new AI policy.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2025/01/removing-barriers-to-american-leadership-in-artificial-intelligence/"]
9. **mid** — OpenAI has released a Responses API, built-in tools including web search, file search, and computer use, and an Agents SDK for orchestrating single-agent and multi-agent workflows, so an agent-building stack is already generally documented for developers before the 2027 horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://openai.com/index/new-tools-for-building-agents/","https://platform.openai.com/docs/guides/agents"]
10. **mid** — Anthropic released Claude computer use in public beta in October 2024, documenting that the model can view a screen, move a cursor, click buttons, and type text through a tool interface, establishing browser/desktop-control capability as an available agent primitive before 2027.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://www.anthropic.com/news/3-5-models-and-computer-use","https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/computer-use/overview"]
11. **mid** — Microsoft announced in October 2024 that autonomous agents in Copilot Studio would move from private preview to public preview at Microsoft Ignite 2024, making enterprise agent creation and management a shipped Microsoft product path before the 2027 horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://blogs.microsoft.com/blog/2024/10/21/new-autonomous-agents-scale-your-team-like-never-before/"]
12. **mid** — GitHub Copilot coding agent is documented as a feature that can be assigned GitHub issues, works in its own development environment, pushes commits, and opens pull requests for human review, so asynchronous software-development agents already exist as a productized workflow before 2027.
   - Resolve by: 2026-09-17; source_refs: ["https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/concepts/about-copilot-coding-agent","https://github.blog/news-insights/product-news/github-copilot-coding-agent-in-public-preview/"]
13. **mid** — OpenAI announced the Stargate Project on 21 January 2025 as a new company intending to invest 500 billion dollars over four years in U.S. AI infrastructure for OpenAI, with 100 billion dollars beginning immediately and initial equity funders including SoftBank, OpenAI, Oracle, and MGX.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://openai.com/index/announcing-the-stargate-project/"]
14. **mid** — OpenAI stated that Arm, Microsoft, NVIDIA, Oracle, and OpenAI are initial technology partners in the Stargate Project, fixing part of the compute-supply consortium available to OpenAI agent products before the 2027 horizon.
   - Resolve by: 2027-09-17; source_refs: ["https://openai.com/index/announcing-the-stargate-project/"]

## Load-bearing uncertainty axes (ADR-006)
These are not determined facts; they are orthogonal dimensions on which 2027-09-17 can genuinely fork.

1. **Agent autonomy ceiling in production software work** — consensus pole: agents remain strongest as scoped copilots/asynchronous junior contributors whose outputs are reviewed by humans, rather than trusted end-to-end owners of major systems.
2. **Enterprise permissioning and liability tolerance** — consensus pole: organizations allow agents to operate inside constrained sandboxes with audit trails, approval gates, and limited credentials, rather than broad unsupervised authority across systems of record.
3. **Compute and model cost trajectory** — consensus pole: frontier-capability agents become cheaper and faster, but high-reliability long-horizon agent runs still face meaningful cost/latency limits and supply concentration.
4. **Regulatory fragmentation versus harmonization** — consensus pole: the EU AI Act and sector/state rules create compliance workstreams, but there is no single globally harmonized agent-governance regime by the horizon.
5. **Security and misuse pressure** — consensus pole: agentic tools materially expand both defensive automation and offensive/scam automation, so security controls and identity/provenance mechanisms become central deployment constraints.

## Bounded deeper exploration: three futures to sample, without predicting
The determined facts above can support three distinct future explorations:
- **Regulated enterprise copilots:** EU/Colorado/NIST baselines and enterprise productization channel agents into auditable workflows with limited autonomy.
- **Software-development acceleration:** GitHub/OpenAI/Anthropic/Microsoft primitives make asynchronous coding and computer-use agents a common development substrate, bounded by review and security gates.
- **Compute-rich frontier agents:** Stargate-style infrastructure and cloud/accelerator consortia expand available capacity for more capable agent services, while cost, safety, and governance remain the sampled uncertainties.

## Load-bearing uncertainty axes (ADR-006)
These are not determined facts; they are orthogonal dimensions on which 2027-09-17 can genuinely fork.

1. **Agent autonomy ceiling in production software work** — consensus pole: agents remain strongest as scoped copilots/asynchronous junior contributors whose outputs are reviewed by humans, rather than trusted end-to-end owners of major systems.
2. **Enterprise permissioning and liability tolerance** — consensus pole: organizations allow agents to operate inside constrained sandboxes with audit trails, approval gates, and limited credentials, rather than broad unsupervised authority across systems of record.
3. **Compute and model cost trajectory** — consensus pole: frontier-capability agents become cheaper and faster, but high-reliability long-horizon agent runs still face meaningful cost/latency limits and supply concentration.
4. **Regulatory fragmentation versus harmonization** — consensus pole: the EU AI Act and sector/state rules create compliance workstreams, but there is no single globally harmonized agent-governance regime by the horizon.
5. **Security and misuse pressure** — consensus pole: agentic tools materially expand both defensive automation and offensive/scam automation, so security controls and identity/provenance mechanisms become central deployment constraints.

## Bounded deeper exploration: three futures to sample, without predicting
The determined facts above can support three distinct future explorations:
- **Regulated enterprise copilots:** EU/Colorado/NIST baselines and enterprise productization channel agents into auditable workflows with limited autonomy.
- **Software-development acceleration:** GitHub/OpenAI/Anthropic/Microsoft primitives make asynchronous coding and computer-use agents a common development substrate, bounded by review and security gates.
- **Compute-rich frontier agents:** Stargate-style infrastructure and cloud/accelerator consortia expand available capacity for more capable agent services, while cost, safety, and governance remain the sampled uncertainties.

forecasts.question: By 2027-06-01, mainstream DevOps and source-control vendors have opened early-access programs in which managed agent principals can satisfy service-ownership or incident-owner requirements for protected production services when the customer's policy envelope specifies budgets, risk classes, required evaluations, rollback paths, audit logging, and escalation thresholds.

By 2027-06-23, a visible cohort of production agent customers has completed at least one 89-to-129-day preview or pilot cycle using those controls for semi-unattended workflows, and procurement/security teams have concrete loss, spend, rollback, escalation, and audit evidence from real deployments. The output is not uniform thresholds such as a universal five-PR cap, but customer-specific numerical budgets and escalation matrices that can be copied into RFPs.

By 2027-09-17, leading agent-platform vendors package governance controls as first-class paid product requirements for unattended or semi-unattended agents, with pricing and sales collateral centered on blast-radius ledgers, independent verifier stages, audit retention, spend caps, sandboxing, reversibility, and human-oversight workflows.

By 2026-12-16, at least three large enterprise software operators have moved beyond ad hoc coding-agent PRs and are running internal design-partner pilots in which agents have named service-captain or service-owner labels, bounded deployment authority, observability access, and mandatory human escalation policies for non-P1 systems.

By 2026-09-17, enterprise risk teams have converted AI, cyber, and software-supply-chain requirements into checklists for autonomous software agents, treating EU AI Act transparency, EU Cyber Resilience Act vulnerability reporting, Colorado high-risk-AI duties, and NIST AI RMF mappings as envelope fields and audit evidence rather than as requirements for human review of every agent output.

By 2026-10-03, at least one top-tier payments or platform company has begun a limited autonomous service-captain trial in which selected P2/P3 services allow agents to triage incidents, merge low-risk changes, and start phased deployments inside the approved authority envelope while humans approve the charter and budget ceiling.

By 2027-06-25, GitHub and PagerDuty open early-access or public-beta enterprise programs for agent service ownership at scale: customers can enroll many repositories or services through templates and APIs, configure agent CODEOWNERS/incident-owner roles, set deployment controls and human escalation conditions, and receive consolidated audit and spend reports.

By 2027-09-17, the enterprise market norm is mainstream-but-bounded agent use: most organizations run at least one production development or business-process agent, but only a small minority permit unsupervised production-code merges or large external payments without human approval.

By 2027-08-22, enterprise RFP templates, cyber/AI-risk questionnaires, and broker/auditor checklists for production agents routinely ask vendors to document blast-radius budgets, independent verification, audit logs, spend caps, sandboxing, reversibility, and human-oversight workflows. This converts the pilot evidence into buyer gating criteria across regulated and ordinary SaaS/cloud-finance purchases.

By 2027-04-28, enough large organizations have at least one bounded agent in a production development or business-process workflow—such as human-reviewed pull-request work, IT/service ticket triage and remediation suggestions, sales/service case handling, finance-document processing, or HR workflow assistance—that cross-industry surveys would honestly report majority production use without counting mere chat-only experimentation.

By 2027-03-26, at least three mainstream cloud, developer-platform, or agent-orchestration ecosystems have customer-visible preview or early-access implementations of the evidence profile: policy envelopes or budget ledgers, audit-log export, sandboxed tool credentials, human-in-the-loop workflow gates, and independent verifier hooks. The implementations are incomplete and differ by vendor, but they make governance controls purchasable line items rather than bespoke consulting work.

By 2027-02-19, both vendors are running private previews with selected enterprise design partners in which managed agent principals can be recorded as delegated owners for low-risk repositories or services, while risky production changes still require policy-specified human approval or escalation.

By 2027-09-15, customer telemetry from early-access and enterprise deployments shows that autonomous service owners have handled millions of incident acknowledgements and hundreds of thousands of code or rollout actions, with severe-incident rates low enough that vendors recommend policy-envelope control, observability, rollback, and post-action audit instead of universal pre-action human approval.

By 2027-02-22, those vendors have integrated the authority-envelope profile into private-beta controls for managed non-human principals, so an approved agent can satisfy selected ownership and workflow gates only when the envelope, automated tests, deployment policy, audit logging, and escalation policy all pass.

By 2027-04-08, at least one visible Workbench-style unattended software-maintenance deployment has produced a multi-repository cascade or comparable business incident, showing that tool-using coding agents can create production risk when CI, policy compilation, secrets-scoped test environments, and auto-approval are connected without an explicit blast-radius budget.

By 2027-01-23, design partners finish the first usable policy-schema and connector prototype for the authority overlay, mapping only existing GitHub repository/ruleset/CODEOWNERS data, PagerDuty service/escalation-policy data, CI/CD environment approvals, secrets scopes, model-provider tenant settings, and budget owners into signed per-service agent envelopes with explicit deny-by-default behavior and human escalation conditions.

EU-focused agent vendors, outside counsel, and audit firms translate the already-applicable AI Act, Data Act, and CRA dates into a common autonomous-agent evidence checklist: exportable event logs and memories, AI-generated-content labels, security incident and vulnerability routing, AI risk-management files, and documented human-oversight mappings.

By 2027-09-17, the public governance norm among leading autonomous-agent platform customers has shifted from human review of each routine agent output toward policy-envelope control: executives and platform teams set scopes, budgets, risk classes, rollback rules, audit logging, and escalation requirements, while agents make routine engineering and production decisions inside those boundaries.

By 2027-06-10, private-preview customers have run the GitHub and PagerDuty overlays on constrained P2/P3/P4 services for at least sixty-nine days, producing audit evidence that agent ownership is mostly a routing, evidence, rollback, and escalation role rather than unfettered autonomous merge authority: most protected-branch merges and production deploys still require existing ruleset approvals or pre-approved rollout classes, and overrides are analyzed in weekly model and control reviews.

By 2027-07-30, pilot evidence from the enrolled enterprises shows that policy-envelope control can replace mandatory human review for large volumes of routine agent pull requests, incident acknowledgements, phased rollouts, Terraform-like bounded infrastructure changes, and rollbacks without waiving executive accountability, audit reconstruction, or acquirer/insurer exception rights.

By 2027-06-10, incident experience, insurance questionnaires, audit reviews, and board policies reinforce a common operating boundary: production-code merges to protected branches and large external payments remain human-approved exceptions, while agents may prepare drafts, run tests, propose changes, route work, and execute low-risk or reversible actions inside pre-scoped systems.

By 2027-03-23, several large enterprises including at least one high-volume payments or commerce operator have started production pilots in which agents make routine P2/P3 engineering and operations decisions inside authority envelopes while P1 emergencies, envelope changes, and unbounded payment-core or regulatory exceptions still escalate to humans.

By 2027-04-08, at least one visible enterprise incident involving unattended software-maintenance agents shows that agent-authored pull requests can pass local CI yet still cause production regressions when automerge authority, issue orchestration, and repair authority are not bounded by blast-radius budgets.

By 2026-10-26, GitHub and PagerDuty enterprise design-partner teams have agreed on a narrow agent-service-owner requirements profile: agent identities are attached to a human owning team, can be named in CODEOWNERS-like or incident-owner fields only for preclassified low-risk scopes, and must carry human escalation conditions rather than replacing all human ownership.

By 2027-03-16, security, legal, and procurement teams at large agent buyers have translated the pilot findings and live EU/NIST compliance baselines into standard questionnaire requirements for agent platforms: immutable logs, human-oversight mapping, budget caps, sandbox boundaries, independent validation, and documented reversibility before any unattended authority is approved.

By 2027-08-31, the early-access cohort has generated enough production evidence for public enterprise launch materials: hundreds of thousands of agent-owned pull requests, thousands of agent-initiated rollbacks, millions of autonomous incident acknowledgements, measured severe-incident rates, median resolution times, customer spend distributions, and documented human-override rates.

By 2027-03-21, at least one high-volume commerce company has completed a major agent-owned production rewrite under an Owner Envelope and its postmortem committee has voted to continue autonomous system ownership for P2-and-lower services, concluding that better tests and envelope controls beat restoring universal human merge approval.

At least one customer-visible unattended-agent failure in a production software or business workflow causes regulated buyers to ask whether agent actions are logged, reversible, human-approved where high risk, and reportable under product-security playbooks.

By 2026-12-16, enterprise design partners for agent-orchestration vendors have completed at least one 90-day controlled pilot connecting coding, browser/computer-use, and business-workflow agents to real repositories or SaaS systems, and their pilot reports identify audit logs, sandbox isolation, approval workflows, spend limits, and action rollback as procurement blockers for unattended use.

By 2027-04-02, GitHub and PagerDuty have separate private-preview implementations of the overlay for named enterprise customers: GitHub exposes managed agent principals as CODEOWNERS-compatible reviewers only within signed envelopes and only with human co-owner or ruleset escape hatches, while PagerDuty exposes agent incident-owner/first-responder roles that can acknowledge, diagnose, roll back approved runbooks, and page humans on severity, uncertainty, spend, or policy-boundary triggers.

By 2027-09-17, GitHub Enterprise Cloud and PagerDuty Operations Cloud publicly offer enterprise autonomous-service-owner products: GitHub supports managed agent CODEOWNERS principals with deployment controls, spend limits, auditability, independent model review, regulatory hooks, and human escalation rules, while PagerDuty supports agent incident-owner integrations with immutable logs, rollback/deployment controls, customer authority envelopes, regulatory mappings, and human sponsor/escalation requirements.

By 2027-03-31, a large minority of mid-market and enterprise buyers have moved at least one bounded development-agent or business-process-agent workflow from pilot into production, concentrated in dependency triage, support drafting, sales research, knowledge retrieval, ticket routing, and test generation where agent actions are reviewable and reversible.

By 2027-03-17, GitHub has a private-preview Copilot Agent Fleet service-ownership implementation for selected Enterprise Cloud customers, allowing managed agent principals to satisfy CODEOWNERS-like ownership checks inside protected repositories when branch protection, required evaluations, deployment protection rules, AI-credit limits, audit trails, second-model review, and escalation rules all pass.

Large EU and multinational buyers update autonomous-agent RFPs, DPAs, security questionnaires, and renewal checklists to require the evidence checklist: exportable logs and switching support, content transparency labeling, incident/vulnerability notification hooks, AI risk files, and human-oversight records.

By 2027-08-21, enterprise buyer surveys and procurement telemetry show agent adoption crossing a mainstream threshold: most surveyed organizations run at least one development or business-process agent in production, while only a small minority permit unsupervised production-code merges or large external payments without a human approval event.

By 2026-10-16, major source-control, incident-management, identity, and payments-platform design partners have agreed on a minimal authority-envelope profile for autonomous software-agent operations: service/repository scope, transaction and spend ceilings, risk class, rollout blast radius, rollback rule, immutable audit trail, human escalation trigger, and named executive/platform owner.

By 2027-03-17, PagerDuty has a private-preview Autonomous Service Owner integration for Operations Cloud design partners, letting approved customer agents acknowledge and resolve incidents, query observability tools, update runbooks, trigger rollback and deployment workflows through connected providers, and preserve 400-day audit logs under customer-defined service, severity, spend, data, and jurisdiction limits.

By 2027-09-17, GitHub Enterprise Cloud and PagerDuty Operations Cloud publicly offer enterprise public-beta products or add-ons for agent service ownership at scale: GitHub supports managed agent CODEOWNERS-like co-owner/reviewer roles inside repository and deployment rulesets, and PagerDuty supports managed agent incident-owner roles inside service and escalation policies; both include deployment controls, audit logs, spend limits, independent model-review artifacts, regulatory hooks, and human escalation conditions.

By 2027-04-29, the private-preview governance package includes exportable audit logs, spend-limit enforcement, regulatory-mapping hooks for NIST AI RMF and EU AI/data/cyber evidence, and independent model review as an auditable secondary check that informs policy gates rather than substituting for human approval on high-risk actions.

By 2027-07-30, vendors running regulated-enterprise betas have accumulated a 90-day evidence window for the new controls, allowing auditors and customers to review verifier independence, log retention, sandbox isolation, incident reporting, and human-oversight evidence rather than relying on demonstrations that agents can merely call tools.

By 2027-05-01, the affected agent-platform vendor and its close competitors have issued emergency unattended-agent controls: hard blast-radius ledgers, per-incident model/tool spend caps, escalation after agent-created defects, mandatory human approval for sensitive domains, and operational circuit breakers tied to step-level audit traces.

By 2026-11-16, GitHub, PagerDuty, and at least three shared enterprise design partners choose a narrow 'authority overlay' architecture for agent service ownership: agents may be listed as co-owners only where a repository or service already has valid human owner, escalation policy, deployment environment, cost center, and data-classification metadata; missing or conflicting metadata blocks agent authority and escalates to the human owner rather than being bulk-imported or inferred.

By 2026-12-14, at least several engineering risk committees at large software firms have approved an Owner Envelope policy: for lower-than-P1 production systems with reproducible builds, bounded rollout blast radius, scoped credentials, required evidence emission, rollback plans, audit logging, and escalation rules, an autonomous agent can be the production owner without human approval of each pull request or deployment.

By 2027-09-17, analyst notes, vendor pricing pages, launch materials, and buyer surveys describe agent platforms primarily in terms of unattended-agent governance controls, with tool-use capability treated as table stakes. The market-wide settlement is visible without requiring one highly specific RelayForge-style all-region GA: multiple vendors sell governance-control SKUs or plan tiers, and buyers compare blast-radius, auditability, spend, sandbox, verifier, reversibility, and human-oversight features as core product requirements.

By 2027-06-01, GitHub Agent Fleet ownership and PagerDuty ASO early-access programs are operating in production at more than 100 combined enterprise customers, with enrolled services limited mostly to P2/P3/P4 workloads and with monthly customer-level caps on model, sandbox, CI, and workflow spend.

By 2027-01-15, GitHub and PagerDuty enterprise product teams have converged with design partners on a common 'authority envelope' requirements set for autonomous service ownership: repository or service scope, incident-owner identity, deployment and rollback bounds, immutable audit logs, usage/spend caps, independent model review gates for sensitive paths, regulatory workflow hooks, and explicit human escalation conditions.

By 2026-12-31, the major enterprise agent vendors and orchestration vendors have packaged agent workflows with admin controls, auditable tool traces, sandboxing, connector permissions, and human-approval gates, so security and procurement teams can approve limited production deployments rather than treating agents only as experiments.

By 2027-05-23, enterprise insurers, auditors, procurement reviewers, and platform trust teams have converged on bounded-autonomy contract language: agents may run production development and operations workflows, but unsupervised production-code merges, production deploys, and external payments over material thresholds require explicit human approval or two-person review.

Agent-orchestration vendors shipping to EU customers make compliance evidence a product feature rather than a bespoke services deliverable, adding or packaging audit-log export, AI Act transparency labels, CRA reporting workflows, Data Act export formats, risk-file archives, and human-oversight evidence before September 2027 procurement decisions close.

By 2027-09-17, the dominant governance pattern for autonomous software agents in large enterprise software organizations has shifted upward from human review of each routine agent output to policy-envelope control: executives and platform teams set scope, budget, risk class, rollback, audit, and escalation rules, and agents make routine engineering and production decisions inside those boundaries.

By 2026-12-15, major agent-platform vendors, audit/advisory teams, and at least twenty design-partner enterprises converge on a minimal agent-control evidence profile for production agents: persistent agent identity, immutable action/replay logs, per-agent spend and action ceilings, sandbox or environment scope, rollback/reversibility evidence, human escalation points, and separate verifier records. This is a cheap market mechanism because it is a reusable checklist and API/log schema rather than a fully built single RelayForge gateway.

By 2026-12-25, GitHub and PagerDuty have working authority-envelope prototypes for that profile, including repository/service scope, environment and deployment gates, audit-event typing, spending ceilings, model-review evidence fields, and escalation-to-human-team metadata.

By 2027-01-22, enterprise risk, procurement, and security teams commonly classify bounded SaaS/coding-agent deployments as extensions of existing SaaS, RPA, ITSM, and DevSecOps controls rather than as fully new high-risk autonomous systems, allowing pilots to move into production when approval gates and audit logs remain enabled.

By 2026-12-06, the major enterprise agent platforms used for software development and business workflows converge on bounded-agency defaults: scoped connectors or repository permissions, per-action approval policies, execution logs, sandboxed workspaces or draft outputs, and administrative enablement rather than unrestricted autonomous action.

By 2027-08-18, GitHub and PagerDuty product, legal, and trust teams approve public-beta enterprise launch language for agent service ownership that avoids treating agents as unsupervised human replacements: the offers explicitly include CODEOWNERS or incident-owner labels, deployment controls, immutable audit logs, spend limits, independent model-review records, AI Act/Cyber Resilience Act/NIST reporting hooks, and mandatory human escalation conditions, while reserving final production accountability to the customer's named human organization.

By 2027-09-16, GitHub Enterprise Cloud and PagerDuty Operations Cloud publicly offer enterprise products that explicitly support delegated agent service ownership at scale, including agent CODEOWNERS or incident-owner roles, deployment controls, audit logs, spend limits, independent model-review hooks, regulatory evidence hooks, and human escalation conditions.
